_doc: Expected output per case id of the input file. A response that differs is a Locust failure (Spec06 §5). 'aggregate' counts every status of the case: the verdict shows the 201 / 409 / 422 mix. No traceId on 409 yet (deferred, Spec07 triage B1). BR-03/BR-04 step 'first' only prepares data: 72 cars and 7 oil-change technicians at Q7 mean another user may already hold the car (422) or the hour (409); that is a valid answer, so the case just stops (continueOn).

cases.goal: Spread booking: a random standard car, oil change, random 15-min slot 8–600 days ahead. Mostly 201 with a real (bay, technician) pair; 409 when every pair is busy, 422 when the same car is already booked then.

Contended booking: everyone wants the next 7 days. These days fill within seconds, so most answers become 409 after max-pairs tries: the conflict path (3 short transactions, 23P01) is measured, and no double booking may get through.
Idempotent retry under load: the SAME request with the SAME Idempotency-Key → the same appointment comes back (201, same id), no second row.
Same car, same time, NEW key → 422 (Spec07 D2) under load: one car cannot be in two bays at once, even when the hub has free pairs.
Start in the past → 400, decided before any candidate read or DB write.
Hydrogen car at the hub → 422: no bay or technician there takes it. The candidate read finds nothing; it must stay cheap and never become a 409 or 5xx under load.
HOT read on the contended days (Q7, oil change, gasoline car, next 7 days): BR-02 bookings bump these days' versions through the relay while customers read them.
